name: Me'paa de Acatepec
catalog_citation: Marlett, Stephen A. y Plácido Neri Remigio (2012). Me'paa de Acatepec. Ilustraciones fonéticas de lenguas amerindias, ed. Stephen A. Marlett. Lima: SIL International y Universidad Ricardo Palma. (Edición preliminar, 8 pp.; lengamer.org/publicaciones/trabajos/…
catalog_locator: p. 7, sections 'Los Tonos' and 'La Prominencia Silábica'; p. 8, 'La Roticización de la Oclusiva Dental Sonora'
catalog_quote: Los Tonos. La presentación de los tonos a continuación presume la presencia de melodías tonales en algunos temas simples. Todas las posibilidades de melodías consistiendo de uno o dos tonos parecen ser bien atestiguadas en los temas con dos sílabas. ... [Melodía: Bajo, Medio, Alto, Bajo-Medio, Bajo-Alto, Medio-Bajo, Medio-Alto, Alto-Bajo, Alto-Medio] ... La Prominencia Silábica. Marlett y Weathers (en preparación) argumentan que las lenguas me phaa generalmente tienen una estructura yámbica, aunque nada precisamente de carácter como "acento" se ha identificado. La última sílaba es más fuerte que las otras, que es un tipo de prominencia. Esta prominencia se refleja en los detalles fonéticos de las consonantes, los cuales se discuten en la sección Convenciones.

audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: (1) The deciding quotation and the domain quotation are verbatim in the held PDF (decoded text), with one locator slip: 'Los Tonos'/'La Prominencia Silábica' are on p.6, not p.7 (Roticización p.8 is right), and the item is 11 pp, not 8. (2) The source is a 2012 JIPA-style phonetic illustration by Marlett, the main Me'phaa phonologist, with a native-speaker co-author - short and 'preliminary' but first-hand and variety-specific. (3) The one clearly better work in Glottolog's list, Cline 2013 (UND MA thesis on the tone system of this exact variety, 215 pp), was not held; it is now fetched sources from a Wayback snapshot of UND Scholarly Commons and read: sect. 1.4.4 'Prominence' (pp. 51-52) repeats the position verbatim in substance - 'no clear evidence of something like stress in Me'phaa', 'right-headed, or iambic, prosodic structure', word-final syllables strong / non-final weak, /d/ -> [r] in w

sources.citation: Cline, Kevin L. 2013. The tone system of Acatepec Me'paa. M.A. thesis, University of North Dakota. xv+199 pp. https://commons.und.edu/theses/1410 (SIL archive entry 57058).
sources.quote: p.51: 'Marlett and Weathers propose that, while there is no clear evidence of something like stress in Meꞌphaa, words and phrases in all varieties demonstrate a right-headed, or iambic, prosodic structure (in preparation:24). Some phonetic details depend on references to a weak syllable. For example, in major class words, the phoneme /d/ is consistently pronounced as [d] when it occurs in the final, strong syllable of disyllabic words ... When it occurs in non-final, weak syllables ... it is pronounced as [r].' fn.5: 'Word-final syllables are strong, while non-final syllables are weak.' p.13:
sources.locator: sect. 1.4.4 'Prominence', pp. 51-52; sect. 1.3.1 p. 13 (three contrastive tone heights); fn. 5 (word-final syllables strong); fn. 9 p. 24; abstract (all nine two-tone melodies on disyllabic nouns)
sources.note: Glottolog's only 'phonology' item for acat1239 and the fullest description of this exact variety; our record rested on an 11-pp preliminary illustration. fetched sources now: sect. 1.4.4 confirms 'no clear evidence of something like stress', right-headed/iambic structure, final syllable strong; three tone heights.
